_why: Panels whose shared chrome and stacked settings column do NOT share one
left edge. Measured 2026-09-07: 35 of the 37 panels that have both were
staggered, from -25px (image) to +78px (breadcrumb), while check:panels
reported a clean pass over all 224 panels.
THAT 35 AND THE 31 NAMES BELOW DO NOT MATCH, and the difference is not
an error in either. The 35 was a hand measurement taken before this
assertion existed; the 31 is what the assertion records. Re-measured
2026-09-08 with the check itself, on the seeded fixture at 1440 / 1600 /
1920, the arithmetic it prints on every run is:
35 module names carry both a chrome strip and a settings column
-1  carousel is SKIPPED -- its column sits BESIDE the chrome, which is
a legitimate side-by-side layout with no shared edge to hold
= 34 compared
-3  feature-cards and program-list already declare the shared lattice
and line up; speech-bubble is comparable on the LABEL track only
(its leftmost column is a single full-width field) and lines up
there, so it is not recorded
= 31 recorded
+1  admin-related-articles, a module that did not exist when the 35 was
measured -- it landed on main 2026-09-08 in PR #658 and has never
been straightened, so the assertion caught it as a new regression on
its first run against it (-6px on the control track; its label track
already lines up). It is recorded here rather than fixed because
straightening a panel is an explicit non-goal of 86bbw8643.
= 32 recorded below
The exact membership of the older 35 is not reproducible from here, so
trust the run over this paragraph: check:panels prints all four numbers,
names the skip and the label-track-only panel, and refuses (exit 2)
rather than passing if it reaches none of them.
This list is a RECORD OF A DEFECT, not a set of exemptions. Ticket
86bbq065f empties it. It may only ever shrink: check_panels fails if a
panel in here lines up (the record is stale) and fails if a panel not in
here is staggered (a new regression).
The two documented chrome exemptions -- the heading and floating-image
chromes -- are NOT in here. They are flowing bars rather than lattice
columns on purpose and carry no .builder-module-chrome strip, so this
assertion never reaches them. See docs/UI_RULES.md.
NO WIDTH DIMENSION, deliberately: an entry is either staggered or it is
not, at every width. These tracks are max-content, so the stagger is
content-driven and identical at 1440 / 1600 / 1920 -- measured, not
assumed. A future width-DEPENDENT stagger would have no passing state
here (stale at the widths where it lines up, a regression at the width
where it does not) and would fail loudly at both ends rather than hide.
Give the entries a per-width shape if that day comes.
